<!-- pr-reviewer: 8207e79e4501cf0e380b5b4697e1662d3e7d8ffb -->
**Verdict: does not merge with current `main` - needs a re-merge of main before review.**

Thank you for the fix for #905. I stopped before building, because the head no longer merges cleanly with `main` at `2437098f` (GitHub's "mergeable" flag still shows the older test merge against `8f64e646`, from before #910 and #880 landed).

**What conflicts, and why**

```
git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main   (on 8207e79e)
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in .claude/PROCESS_VERSION
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in xtask/src/tests.rs
```

Neither file is changed by this PR. The branch now has two merge bases with `main` (`bac4d015` and `cdc43fd4`, the fork's `chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION 14`, which reached `main` through #910). Git's virtual merge base then puts 14 against 15 against 16 in `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, and in `xtask/src/tests.rs` it is missing the `packaging_build_clears_compiler_wrappers` test (#935).

**Requested before merge**

1. Merge `upstream/main` into `issue/905-arc-corner-gouge` (a merge, not a rebase) and take main's side of both files: `git checkout --theirs .claude/PROCESS_VERSION xtask/src/tests.rs` (the result is `16`, and the file keeps the #935 test). Then push. The PR's own five files (`arc_wall.rs`, `section.rs`, `verify/mod.rs`, `boundary_arc_walls.rs` and the decision file) merge cleanly and need no changes.

**Notes (non-blocking)**

- This PR changes the gouge law (it is under the safety floor), so the next head gets a full review: the build, `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --tests`, and the app suites `boundary_arc_walls`, `verify_arc_reading`, `wall_arc_entry`, `solid_law`, `solid_law_goldens`, `shoulder_adaptive`, `golden_cl` and `conformance`, plus clippy and a scratch check of the arc-to-corner geometry in both directions. None of that ran on this head.
- Open draft PR #911 also edits `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs`. Whichever merges second may need a small re-merge there.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 8207e79e4501cf0e380b5b4697e1662d3e7d8ffb -->
**This review replaces my earlier comment on this head.** That comment's "conflicts" verdict was a false alarm. The local conflict came from the branch having two merge bases with `main`, and it touched only `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` and `xtask/src/tests.rs`, which this PR does not change. GitHub merges the head cleanly.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

## What looks good
- `Trace::of` follows `cl::arc_chords`'s own rules for degenerate arcs: zero radius or zero sweep reads as the straight chord, and full circles never reach a move. A non-finite centre or radius fails closed (`Trace::Unread` reads as near). A NaN distance also reads near (`ge(&floor).not()`).
- The distance geometry in `arc_wall.rs` is sound:
  - The breaks at the lines through the centre and each arc end split the edge into pieces that lie wholly inside or wholly outside the wedge.
  - A piece's `|CP|` range is the clamped perpendicular foot up to its farther end, and the gap is measured to the `ARC_PAD` band.
  - Outside the wedge, the endpoint distances cover it.
  - Arcs over a half turn and arcs across the 0 / pi angle wrap are handled by `rem_euclid`.
- No unchecked divisions: `o0 != o1` guards the break, and `dd > EPSILON` guards the foot. There is no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests.
- The verdict can only grow. The joint reading (`gouged`, including #839's union) is computed first and left as it was; the whole-arc reading only ORs onto it (`section.rs:113-117`). Area mode is untouched, and straight moves keep the same squared comparison.
- No golden or snapshot changes. Provenance lines are on the new module and on the suite. Files are 234 / 288 / 158 lines. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #905`. No process files are touched.

## Local results (head 8207e79e merged with main 2437098f)
The local trial merge took main's side of the two process files.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --tests` | all green: lib 70 (with `the_exact_distance_matches_a_dense_sampling`) plus 28 suites |
| app `boundary_arc_walls` | 3 passed |
| app `verify_arc_reading` | 6 passed |
| app `wall_arc_entry` | 7 passed |
| app `solid_law` | 4 passed |
| app `solid_law_goldens` | 1 passed |
| app `shoulder_adaptive` | 3 passed |
| app `golden_cl` | 25 passed |
| app `conformance` | 6 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I also ran my own scratch suite (deleted afterwards, never pushed); all 7 tests pass. Every case below ran both CW and CCW:
- **Corners along the sweep:** a corner at 10 %, 50 % and 90 % of the sweep, outside and inside the circle, on arcs starting at 0, at 3 rad, across angle 0 and across pi. All are convicted at 3.5 / 3.9 / 3.985 mm and all are clean at 3.995 / 4.0 / 4.3 mm (floor 3.99).
- **Beyond the arc's end:** a corner on the circle's continuation 4.3 mm past the arc's end is clean.
- **Helix:** a helical arc (z -1 to -3) is convicted at 3.9 and clean at 4.2.
- **Finishing ring:** 8 arcs inside a circumscribed 256-gon wall exactly R off are clean. The same ring 0.02 mm too large convicts all 8.
- **Lead-in arc:** a lead-in arc tangent to a straight wall is clean, both as a quarter turn and as a half turn. Moved 0.05 mm toward the wall, it is convicted.
- **Chord side:** an island edge on the chord side of a 0.2 rad arc, 4.2 mm off, is clean.
- **Degenerate arcs:** a zero radius, a zero sweep, from == to, and NaN or infinite centres. None panic.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (non-blocking)
- **Cost.** Each arc is read against every region and section edge, with no spatial pre-filter. That is O(moves x edges), the same edge walk the straight-move reading (#43) already does, so it is not new quadratic cost. `dist_seg` allocates a small `Vec` per edge (`arc_wall.rs:135`). A fixed `[f64; 4]` buffer would avoid that on long programs.
- **XZ/YZ arcs.** They still get only the joint reading (documented in the decision file). A follow-up issue could track it if those arcs ever run in Boundary mode next to walls.
- **Model-backed case.** No new test covers a section edge, or a region edge the probe classifies as a wall. The classification code is unchanged, and the model-backed suites pass.
- **Test placement.** `crates/app/tests/boundary_arc_walls.rs` uses only the `verify` re-exports. It could live in `crates/sim/tests/`, next to the crate that owns the behaviour.
- **Draft #911.** I trial-merged it with this head (`git merge-tree`): it merges cleanly, with no textual conflict in `section.rs`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
